12	// Reading rules for a saved trusted-setup record.
13	//
14	// A setup belongs exclusively to the frozen circuit version named in the
15	// record, and both members that pin that binding carry a uniqueness rule. The
16	// "version" is the sole authority for which version the setup is for, and the
17	// "name" is the sole authority for which circuit owns it: just as a doubled
18	// version could rebind the setup across two frozen versions of one circuit, a
19	// doubled circuit name (canonical "name" beside an ASCII case variant such as
20	// "NAME") would let encoding/json keep the last value and rebind a setup
21	// registered only for circuit a onto a likewise-frozen circuit b. This file
22	// gives the directory scan one per-record reader for the envelope's "setups"
23	// array (scanSetupArray) so that, just as for job records, every spelling the
24	// ordinary struct decode fills Version or Name from counts as that one field
25	// and may appear at most once in a record.
26	//
27	// Keys reach every rule below already JSON-unescaped, so a key written with a
28	// \uXXXX escape is judged on its decoded spelling too. Only the name and
29	// version fields get these uniqueness rules; a setup record's other members
30	// keep their prior reading behavior.
31	
32	type persistSetup struct {
33		Name    string `json:"name"`
34		Version int    `json:"version"`
35	}
36	
37	// setupNameKey is the canonical wire spelling of the field naming the circuit
38	// a setup belongs to.
39	const setupNameKey = "name"
40	
41	// isSetupNameKey reports whether key names a setup record's owning-circuit
42	// field under any spelling the ordinary struct decode fills Name from:
43	// canonical "name" or an ASCII letter-case variant such as "NAME" or "NaMe",
44	// including a JSON-escaped spelling that unescapes onto either (keys arrive
45	// here already unescaped). No non-ASCII rune case-folds onto any letter of
46	// "name" under encoding/json's Unicode-folded tag matching either, so the
47	// ASCII fold recognizes exactly the keys that bind to the field.
48	func isSetupNameKey(key string) bool {
49		return isASCIIFoldOf(key, setupNameKey)
50	}
51	
52	// rejectAmbiguousSetupName enforces the owning-circuit-name uniqueness rule on
53	// one saved setup record: the name decides which circuit the setup belongs to,
54	// so one record may carry the field under at most one recognized spelling
55	// (isSetupNameKey) — canonical "name", an ASCII letter-case variant, or a
56	// JSON-escaped spelling that unescapes onto either. Two spellings on one record
57	// make the owning circuit depend on key order, since encoding/json keeps the
58	// last value, and corrupt the whole directory read: the record is refused
59	// whether the two values agree or differ (a setup registered only for a whose
60	// record also names b is exactly the dangerous case, with a and b both frozen
61	// at version 1), whether both name circuits that exist and are frozen, whether
62	// the two keys are adjacent or the version sits between them, and in whichever
63	// key order they appear. A record carrying only case variants with no
64	// lowercase "name" ("NAME" beside "Name", …) is refused on the same terms, and
65	// two byte-identical spellings are covered as well. A single spelling of any
66	// recognized kind is the one name field and keeps its current reading.
67	//
68	// keys are the record's member keys in any order; the recognized spellings are
69	// filtered and sorted here so the message is deterministic. where names the
70	// record positionally ("setup record #<1-based index>"): the record refuses to
71	// settle which circuit it belongs to, so the finding is never attributed to
72	// either candidate name.
73	func rejectAmbiguousSetupName(where string, keys []string) error {
74		var nameKeys []string
75		for _, key := range keys {
76			if isSetupNameKey(key) {
77				nameKeys = append(nameKeys, key)
78			}
79		}
80		if len(nameKeys) <= 1 {

82		}
83		sort.Strings(nameKeys)

85		for i, k := range nameKeys {

87		}
88		return corruptf("%s carries the circuit name field %q more than once (as %s); the circuit a trusted setup belongs to must not depend on field order",
89			where, setupNameKey, strings.Join(quoted, ", "))
90	}
91	
92	// setupVersionKey is the canonical wire spelling of the field naming the
93	// circuit version a setup belongs to.
94	const setupVersionKey = "version"
95	
96	// isSetupVersionKey reports whether key names a setup record's version field
97	// under any spelling the ordinary struct decode fills Version from: canonical
98	// "version", an ASCII letter-case variant such as "VERSION" or "VeRsIoN", or a
99	// JSON-escaped spelling that unescapes onto either. Because encoding/json's
100	// struct-tag matching folds with Unicode case rules (strings.EqualFold), the
101	// long-s "verſion" (U+017F, written directly or as the u017f escape) names
102	// the field too.
103	func isSetupVersionKey(key string) bool {
104		return strings.EqualFold(key, setupVersionKey)
105	}
106	
107	// rejectAmbiguousSetupVersion enforces the version uniqueness rule on one
108	// saved setup record: the version decides which frozen circuit version the
109	// setup belongs to, so one record may carry the field under at most one
110	// recognized spelling (isSetupVersionKey) — canonical "version", an ASCII
111	// letter-case variant, a JSON-escaped spelling, or the Unicode-folded long-s
112	// "verſion" (U+017F). Two spellings on one record make the bound version
113	// depend on key order, since encoding/json keeps the last value, and corrupt
114	// the whole directory read: the record is refused whether the two values agree
115	// or differ (both 1 and 2 frozen with setups is exactly the dangerous case),
116	// whether both are legal versions, whether unrelated members such as the name
117	// sit between them, and in whichever key order they appear. A record carrying
118	// only case variants with no lowercase "version" is refused on the same terms,
119	// and two byte-identical spellings are covered as well. A single spelling of
120	// any recognized kind — including a lone long-s "verſion" — is the one
121	// version field and keeps its current reading.
122	//
123	// keys are the record's member keys in any order; the recognized spellings are
124	// filtered and sorted here so the message is deterministic. where names the
125	// record positionally ("setup record #<1-based index>"): the record refuses to
126	// settle which version it is, so the finding is never attributed to either
127	// candidate value.
128	func rejectAmbiguousSetupVersion(where string, keys []string) error {
129		var versionKeys []string
130		for _, key := range keys {
131			if isSetupVersionKey(key) {
132				versionKeys = append(versionKeys, key)
133			}
134		}
135		if len(versionKeys) <= 1 {
136			return nil
137		}
138		sort.Strings(versionKeys)
139		quoted := make([]string, len(versionKeys))
140		for i, k := range versionKeys {
141			quoted[i] = strconv.Quote(k)
142		}
143		return corruptf("%s carries the version field %q more than once (as %s); the circuit version a trusted setup belongs to must not depend on field order",

145	}
146	
147	// scanSetupArray consumes one "setups" value positioned at its opening bracket
148	// and reads every record through its own per-record engine, naming each
149	// structural problem, repeated member key or ambiguous name/version field
150	// before the scan moves on. It is the setup counterpart of scanJobArray and
151	// scanCircuitArray: a problem inside one setup is attributed to that record by
152	// its 1-based position ("setup record #n") rather than to an opaque "setups"
153	// element index. A null array stays the pre-existing "no setups" reading.
154	func scanSetupArray(dec *json.Decoder) error {
155		tok, err := dec.Token()
156		if err != nil {
157			return corruptf("data file envelope field \"setups\" is not valid JSON: %v", err)
158		}
159		if tok == nil { // null: json.Unmarshal would produce no setups
160			return nil
161		}
162		if tok != json.Delim('[') {
163			return corruptf("data file envelope field \"setups\" must be an array")
164		}
165		index := 0
166		for dec.More() {
167			index++
168			var raw json.RawMessage
169			if err := dec.Decode(&raw); err != nil {
170				return corruptf("data file envelope field \"setups\" is not valid JSON: %v", err)
171			}
172			positional := fmt.Sprintf("setup record #%d", index)
173			if err := judgeSetupRecord(raw, positional, index); err != nil {
174				return err
175			}
176		}
177		if closeTok, err := dec.Token(); err != nil || closeTok != json.Delim(']') {
178			return corruptf("data file envelope field \"setups\" is not valid JSON")
179		}
180		return nil
181	}
182	
183	// judgeSetupRecord applies the scan-owned rules to one setups element already
184	// captured whole. elementIndex names nested container elements the same way
185	// the envelope-wide recursive scanner did ("setups" element #n).
186	//
187	// A null or scalar element (a number, a string, …) is structurally legal JSON
188	// and stays left to the typed decode and validateEnvelope, which already
189	// reject it; only object and array elements carry member keys to judge. For an
190	// object the shallow member keys drive the name and version uniqueness rules,
191	// and every member value — plus a nested array element — is still walked for
192	// its own duplicate keys, so the scan loses none of the envelope-wide
193	// repeated-key coverage it had through skipValueWithDupKeys.
194	func judgeSetupRecord(raw json.RawMessage, positional string, elementIndex int) error {
195		trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(raw)
196		if len(trimmed) == 0 {
197			return corruptf("%s is not valid JSON", positional)
198		}
199		switch trimmed[0] {
200		case '{':
201			// Decode below names findings as they fall through.
202		case '[':
203			// An array where a record should be can never type-decode; keep the
204			// recursive duplicate-key walk with its historical naming.
205			what := fmt.Sprintf("data file envelope field \"setups\" element #%d", elementIndex)
206			return skipValueWithDupKeys(json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(trimmed)), what)
207		default:
208			return nil // null or a scalar: typing/validation rejects it as before
209		}
210	
211		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(trimmed))
212		open, err := dec.Token()
213		if err != nil || open != json.Delim('{') {
214			return corruptf("%s is not valid JSON", positional)
215		}
216		var keys []string
217		seenExact := make(map[string]bool)
218		dupKey := ""
219		var nestedErr error
220		for dec.More() {
221			keyTok, err := dec.Token()
222			if err != nil {
223				return corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: %v", positional, err)
224			}
225			key, ok := keyTok.(string)
226			if !ok {
227				return corruptf("%s is not valid JSON", positional)
228			}
229			var value json.RawMessage
230			if err := dec.Decode(&value); err != nil {
231				return corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: %v", positional, err)
232			}
233			// The name and version ambiguities outrank an exact repetition of
234			// another member, matching the job record precedence; the first exact
235			// repeated key is remembered for the subsequent finding.
236			if seenExact[key] && dupKey == "" {
237				dupKey = key
238			}
239			seenExact[key] = true
240			keys = append(keys, key)
241			// Setup members are scalars as written, but a hand-edited member may
242			// carry an object/array whose own duplicate keys must still fail the
243			// directory read.
244			v := bytes.TrimSpace(value)
245			if nestedErr == nil && len(v) > 0 && (v[0] == '{' || v[0] == '[') {
246				nestedErr = skipValueWithDupKeys(json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(v)),
247					positional+" field "+strconv.Quote(key))
248			}
249		}
250		if closeTok, err := dec.Token(); err != nil || closeTok != json.Delim('}') {
251			return corruptf("%s is not valid JSON", positional)
252		}
253		if err := rejectAmbiguousSetupName(positional, keys); err != nil {
254			return err
255		}
256		if err := rejectAmbiguousSetupVersion(positional, keys); err != nil {
257			return err
258		}
259		if dupKey != "" {
260			return corruptf("%s contains duplicate field %q", positional, dupKey)
261		}
262		if nestedErr != nil {
263			return nestedErr
264		}
265		return nil
266	}

1	package zkcircuit
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"strconv"
10		"unicode/utf8"
11	)
12	
13	// Saved circuit records used to be read and field-checked twice: once while
14	// the committed envelope was tokenized to reject a repeated object key
15	// (scanCircuitArray) and again while each circuits element was decoded into a
16	// persistCircuit (persistCircuit.UnmarshalJSON). Each pass gathered the
17	// record's member keys on its own and carried its own copy of the object,
18	// required-field and duplicate-key rules, so the judgment of what one
19	// committed circuit record may look like lived in two places that had to
20	// agree by construction.
21	//
22	// This file is now the single home of a saved circuit record's reading rules:
23	// the persistCircuit shape, the exact member spellings it accepts
24	// (name / version / constraints / public_inputs / private_inputs / frozen /
25	// description, plus the one optional definition), the strict scalar typing
26	// and the name exact-readback rule, together with one per-record reading
27	// engine (readCircuitRecord) both read passes drive. The directory scan and
28	// the single-record decode hence tokenize one record once and judge its keys
29	// and structure through the same code, which also covers two byte-identical
30	// member keys — a case a post-decode member map could not see on its own.
31	//
32	// Circuit fields are stricter than envelope and job fields: they are
33	// recognized ONLY under their exact lowercase wire spellings. Keys reach
34	// every rule below already JSON-unescaped, so a key written with a \uXXXX
35	// escape is judged on its decoded spelling, but no letter-case folding is
36	// applied — "FROZEN", "Name" and a long-s lookalike such as "frozeſ" are all
37	// ordinary unknown fields and corrupt the read the same way "note" does.
38	//
39	// Only the reading of saved circuit records is consolidated here. The public
40	// behavior — which values load, which are refused, how the failure is located
41	// and in what order findings surface — is unchanged; the commands, the Go
42	// entry points and the on-disk format stay as they were. In particular the
43	// two read passes keep their historical division of labor and precedence
44	// because an open always runs the directory scan before the typed decode: the
45	// scan owns structural findings and exact repeated keys (readCircuitRecord as
46	// driven by scanCircuitArray) over every record first, while the typed decode
47	// owns unknown fields, the per-field required/type checks, the name
48	// exact-readback rule and the definition decode (decodeCircuit).
49	
50	type persistCircuit struct {
51		Name          string             `json:"name"`
52		Version       int                `json:"version"`
53		Constraints   int                `json:"constraints"`
54		PublicInputs  int                `json:"public_inputs"`
55		PrivateInputs int                `json:"private_inputs"`
56		Frozen        bool               `json:"frozen"`
57		Description   string             `json:"description"`
58		Definition    *persistDefinition `json:"definition,omitempty"`
59	}
60	
61	// persistCircuitFields are the eight fields a committed circuit record may
62	// carry, under their exact (standard lowercase) wire spellings. Seven are
63	// required with the exact JSON type the writer emits; definition alone is
64	// optional (absent or null both mean the legacy counts-only state).
65	var persistCircuitFields = []string{
66		"name", "version", "constraints", "public_inputs", "private_inputs",
67		"frozen", "description", "definition",
68	}
69	
70	// storedRecordShape is the shared strict-JSON rule set (definition_schema.go)
71	// tagged for committed data: every structural failure in a stored circuit or
72	// job record is data corruption, never a bad request.
73	var storedRecordShape = jsonShape{fail: corruptf}
74	
75	// circuitMember is one member of a saved circuit record as seen during the
76	// single per-record pass: its already-JSON-unescaped key and its raw value.
77	type circuitMember struct {
78		key   string
79		value json.RawMessage
80	}
81	
82	// readCircuitRecord consumes exactly one circuit record value the decoder is
83	// positioned at — including its opening token — and returns the members. The
84	// two passes drive it with a different key rule, so one tokenization serves
85	// both historical tiers:
86	//
87	//   - The directory scan passes allowedFields == nil: it does not judge which
88	//     keys are valid, only structure and a repeated key of ANY spelling. That
89	//     matches the old envelope scan, which attributed a repeated member to the
90	//     record whether or not the name was known.
91	//   - The typed decode passes the eight allowed spellings: at each key
92	//     position an unknown spelling is named first and a repeated allowed key
93	//     second, in document order — the precedence of the old strict member
94	//     walk (so an unknown member appearing before another key's second
95	//     occurrence is named as unknown, and an unknown key appearing twice is
96	//     named as unknown rather than duplicate).
97	//
98	// In both tiers the key judgment happens before that occurrence's value is
99	// decoded, the point at which both old passes rejected, so a malformed value
100	// following the offending key never substitutes a syntax error. Every other
101	// token is consumed unless the record is damaged. A null element or a
102	// non-object element is structural damage named by positional. positional is
103	// the name used to locate the record: the directory scan passes
104	// "circuit record #<1-based index>", the typed decode passes
105	// "stored circuit record".
106	//
107	// Member values are captured whole without descending: a nested value such as
108	// the constraint definition owns its own (more precise) strict decoder
109	// during the typed decode.
110	func readCircuitRecord(dec *json.Decoder, positional string, allowedFields []string) ([]circuitMember, error) {
111		open, err := dec.Token()
112		if err != nil {
113			return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: %v", positional, err)
114		}
115		if open == nil {
116			return nil, corruptf("%s must be a JSON object, not null", positional)
117		}
118		if open != json.Delim('{') {
119			return nil, corruptf("%s must be a JSON object", positional)
120		}
121	
122		var allowed map[string]bool
123		if allowedFields != nil {
124			allowed = make(map[string]bool, len(allowedFields))
125			for _, f := range allowedFields {
126				allowed[f] = true
127			}
128		}
129		var members []circuitMember
130		seen := make(map[string]bool)
131		for dec.More() {
132			keyTok, err := dec.Token()
133			if err != nil {
134				return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: %v", positional, err)
135			}
136			key, ok := keyTok.(string)
137			if !ok {
138				return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON", positional)
139			}
140			// Keys arrive already JSON-unescaped, so a key spelled through a
141			// \uXXXX escape is judged on its decoded spelling. The typed tier
142			// names an unknown spelling ahead of a repetition; the scan tier only
143			// sees repetitions. Both judgments pre-date the value decode, as they
144			// always did.
145			if allowed != nil && !allowed[key] {
146				return nil, corruptf("%s has unknown field %q", positional, key)
147			}
148			if seen[key] {
149				return nil, corruptf("%s contains duplicate field %q", positional, key)
150			}
151			seen[key] = true
152			var value json.RawMessage
153			if err := dec.Decode(&value); err != nil {
154				return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: %v", positional, err)
155			}
156			members = append(members, circuitMember{key: key, value: value})
157		}
158		if closeTok, err := dec.Token(); err != nil || closeTok != json.Delim('}') {
159			return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON", positional)
160		}
161		return members, nil
162	}
163	
164	// scanCircuitArray consumes one "circuits" value positioned at its opening
165	// bracket and reads every record through the shared per-record engine in
166	// scan mode (no allowed-field list), which names each structural problem or
167	// repeated key before the scan moves on. It is the directory-wide pre-check
168	// counterpart of decodeCircuit and exists so a structural problem inside one
169	// circuit is attributed to that record by its 1-based position rather than to
170	// an opaque "circuits" element index. A null array stays the pre-existing
171	// "no records" reading.
172	func scanCircuitArray(dec *json.Decoder) error {
173		tok, err := dec.Token()
174		if err != nil {
175			return corruptf("data file envelope field \"circuits\" is not valid JSON: %v", err)
176		}
177		if tok == nil { // null: json.Unmarshal would produce no records
178			return nil
179		}
180		if tok != json.Delim('[') {
181			return corruptf("data file envelope field \"circuits\" must be an array")
182		}
183		index := 0
184		for dec.More() {
185			index++
186			if _, err := readCircuitRecord(dec, fmt.Sprintf("circuit record #%d", index), nil); err != nil {
187				return err
188			}
189		}
190		if closeTok, err := dec.Token(); err != nil || closeTok != json.Delim(']') {
191			return corruptf("data file envelope field \"circuits\" is not valid JSON")
192		}
193		return nil
194	}
195	
196	// Strict decoding of committed circuit records.
197	//
198	// A circuit record in data.json must name each of name, version, constraints,
199	// public_inputs, private_inputs, frozen and description exactly once, with
200	// the exact JSON type the writer emits (string / integer / integer / integer
201	// / integer / boolean / string). A missing key, a null, a wrong type or a
202	// repeated key is data corruption and refuses the whole directory read: a
203	// missing or null frozen flag must not silently read as false (turning a
204	// frozen version back into an editable draft), and a repeated key must not
205	// resolve to its last value. An explicit 0, false or "" is an ordinary value
206	// and stays legal. The definition member remains the one optional field: it
207	// may be absent or null (the legacy counts-only state, which still compiles
208	// no further than "constraint definition missing"); when present it goes
209	// through the strict persistDefinition decoder, keeping the constraint order,
210	// input layout and compiled hash of defined versions intact.
211	//
212	// The name field carries one rule beyond shape: its raw JSON string token
213	// must denote its value exactly — valid UTF-8 in the literal portions and no
214	// unpaired \uXXXX surrogate escapes (checkStoredStringEncoding). Both damage
215	// shapes decode to U+FFFD replacement characters under encoding/json, which
216	// would rename the circuit on read; they are data corruption, and the whole
217	// directory read is refused. Only the name is judged this way; every other
218	// field keeps the ordinary decoding rules.
219	//
220	// Only shape is judged here. The domain rules (non-blank name, positive
221	// version and constraint count, non-negative input counts) keep being
222	// re-checked by validateEnvelope.
223	
224	func (c *persistCircuit) UnmarshalJSON(raw []byte) error {
225		const what = "stored circuit record"
226		return decodeCircuit(raw, what, c)
227	}
228	
229	// decodeCircuit reads one saved circuit record from raw through the shared
230	// engine and fills out. what is the generic name for a record located
231	// positionally; the envelope read prefixes it with the record index when it
232	// re-tags the error.
233	//
234	// Findings surface in the fixed order the two historical passes produced
235	// together: the object gate and trailing data, then the first unknown or
236	// repeated member in document order (an unknown spelling is named before a
237	// repetition at the same key position, exactly as the old strict member walk
238	// ordered it), then the field-by-field required/type checks with the name
239	// encoding rule right after the name string read, and only then the optional
240	// definition's own decode.
241	func decodeCircuit(raw []byte, what string, out *persistCircuit) error {
242		trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(raw)
243		if len(trimmed) == 0 {
244			return corruptf("%s must be a JSON object", what)
245		}
246		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(trimmed))
247		memberList, err := readCircuitRecord(dec, what, persistCircuitFields)
248		if err != nil {
249			return err
250		}
251	
252		// A single complete object is the whole record. Unknown and repeated
253		// members were already rejected during the single tokenization above, in
254		// the old strict-member order (unknown before repetition, in document
255		// order); this trailing-data check follows that gate, exactly as before.
256		// At open the directory scan already guarantees it; the check keeps the
257		// single-record decoder self-contained.
258		if _, err := dec.Token(); err != io.EOF {
259			return corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: trailing data after the object", what)
260		}
261	
262		var c persistCircuit
263	
264		// The members are the allowed spellings without repeats, so the strict
265		// required/scalar reads can address them by name.
266		members := make(map[string]json.RawMessage, len(memberList))
267		for _, m := range memberList {
268			members[m.key] = m.value
269		}
270	
271		requireString := func(key string, dst *string) error {
272			v, err := storedRecordShape.require(members, key, what)
273			if err != nil {
274				return err
275			}
276			s, err := storedRecordShape.string(v, what+" field "+strconv.Quote(key))
277			if err != nil {
278				return err
279			}
280			*dst = s
281			return nil
282		}
283		requireInt := func(key string, dst *int) error {
284			v, err := storedRecordShape.require(members, key, what)
285			if err != nil {
286				return err
287			}
288			n, err := storedRecordShape.int(v, what+" field "+strconv.Quote(key))
289			if err != nil {
290				return err
291			}
292			*dst = n
293			return nil
294		}
295	
296		if err := requireString("name", &c.Name); err != nil {
297			return err
298		}
299		// The name is the version's identity and must read back as the exact
300		// value that was committed. encoding/json silently rewrites both invalid
301		// UTF-8 bytes and unpaired \uXXXX surrogate escapes to U+FFFD, so the
302		// decoded string alone cannot tell a damaged name apart from one that
303		// legitimately contains "�". Judge the raw JSON token instead.
304		if err := checkStoredStringEncoding(members["name"], what+` field "name"`, "committed name"); err != nil {
305			return err
306		}
307		if err := requireInt("version", &c.Version); err != nil {
308			return err
309		}
310		if err := requireInt("constraints", &c.Constraints); err != nil {
311			return err
312		}
313		if err := requireInt("public_inputs", &c.PublicInputs); err != nil {
314			return err
315		}
316		if err := requireInt("private_inputs", &c.PrivateInputs); err != nil {
317			return err
318		}
319		frozenRaw, err := storedRecordShape.require(members, "frozen", what)
320		if err != nil {
321			return err
322		}
323		c.Frozen, err = storedRecordShape.bool(frozenRaw, what+" field "+strconv.Quote("frozen"))
324		if err != nil {
325			return err
326		}
327		if err := requireString("description", &c.Description); err != nil {
328			return err
329		}
330	
331		// definition is the only optional member: absent or null both mean the
332		// counts-only legacy state.
333		if defRaw, present := members["definition"]; present {
334			if string(bytes.TrimSpace(defRaw)) != "null" {
335				var def persistDefinition
336				if err := json.Unmarshal(defRaw, &def); err != nil {
337					var se StoreError
338					if errors.As(err, &se) {
339						return err // already reported as data corruption
340					}
341					return corruptf("%s field %s is not a valid constraint definition: %v", what, strconv.Quote("definition"), err)
342				}
343				c.Definition = &def
344			}
345		}
346	
347		*out = c
348		return nil
349	}
350	
351	// checkStoredStringEncoding enforces an identity field's exact-readback rule
352	// on the raw JSON string token of a committed value (a circuit record's name,
353	// a job record's id). The string has already been decoded by the strict
354	// member read, so the token is known to be one complete, well-formed JSON
355	// string; this walk judges only what that decode silently repairs:
356	//
357	//   - invalid UTF-8 bytes in the literal (unescaped) portions — a lone
358	//     continuation byte, a truncated multi-byte character, an overlong
359	//     form — which encoding/json rewrites to U+FFFD, and
360	//   - \uXXXX escapes forming an unpaired surrogate — a high surrogate not
361	//     immediately followed by its low-surrogate escape, or a low surrogate
362	//     standing alone — which are rewritten to U+FFFD the same way.
363	//
364	// Both would make the record read back under a different value than the bytes
365	// on disk carry, so the record is data corruption rather than a value that
366	// legitimately decodes to a replacement character it never had. noun is the
367	// word naming the value in diagnostics ("committed name" / "committed job
368	// id"); what locates the record and field, e.g.
369	// `stored circuit record field "name"` or `stored job record "j1" field
370	// "id"`. A legal surrogate pair decodes to its astral character, an actually
371	// committed "�" (written directly or as a U+FFFD escape) is an ordinary
372	// value, and the literal six characters "\uD800" — written with an escaped
373	// backslash — carry no escape at all: all three keep their exact value.
374	func checkStoredStringEncoding(raw json.RawMessage, what, noun string) error {
375		token := bytes.TrimSpace(raw)
376		// The token is a complete JSON string (the strict string read above
377		// succeeded), so every escape is well-formed and the walk stays in
378		// bounds; only the replacement-prone content is judged.
379		for i := 1; i < len(token)-1; {
380			c := token[i]
381			if c == '\\' {
382				if token[i+1] != 'u' {
383					i += 2 // a simple escape: \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t
384					continue
385				}
386				code, _ := strconv.ParseUint(string(token[i+2:i+6]), 16, 32)
387				switch {
388				case code >= 0xD800 && code <= 0xDBFF:
389					// A high surrogate is whole only when its low-surrogate
390					// escape follows immediately.
391					if i+12 <= len(token) && token[i+6] == '\\' && token[i+7] == 'u' {
392						lo, _ := strconv.ParseUint(string(token[i+8:i+12]), 16, 32)
393						if lo >= 0xDC00 && lo <= 0xDFFF {
394							i += 12
395							continue
396						}
397					}
398					return corruptf("%s contains an unpaired high surrogate escape (\\u%04X); the %s would not read back unchanged", what, code, noun)
399				case code >= 0xDC00 && code <= 0xDFFF:
400					return corruptf("%s contains an unpaired low surrogate escape (\\u%04X); the %s would not read back unchanged", what, code, noun)
401				}
402				i += 6
403				continue
404			}
405			if c < utf8.RuneSelf {
406				i++
407				continue
408			}
409			r, size := utf8.DecodeRune(token[i:])
410			if r == utf8.RuneError && size == 1 {
411				return corruptf("%s contains invalid UTF-8 bytes; the %s would not read back unchanged", what, noun)
412			}
413			i += size
414		}
415		return nil
416	}

33	// which values load, which are refused, how the failure is located and in

39	// ambiguities, exact repeated keys and nested repeated keys
40	// (jobRecordScan.judge), while the typed decode owns the
41	// binding-field lookalike, duplicate-binding and binding-value-type findings

47		Version  int    `json:"version"`
48		Kind     string `json:"kind"`
49		Attempt  int    `json:"attempt"`

56	// The canonical spellings of the job-record fields the read path treats by
57	// rule rather than leaving entirely to a plain struct decode. Keys reach
58	// every rule below already JSON-unescaped, so a key written with a \uXXXX
59	// escape is judged on its decoded spelling too.
60	const (
61		jobIDKey        = "id"
62		jobCircuitKey   = "circuit"
63		jobVersionKey   = "version"
64		compiledHashKey = "compiled_hash"
65	)

67	// isASCIIFoldOf reports whether key names canonical under an ASCII-only
68	// letter-case fold: the two must have the same byte length and every byte
69	// must match after mapping A-Z onto a-z. A key of a different length, or one
70	// that needs a non-ASCII rune to match, returns false — use strings.EqualFold
71	// to detect those non-ASCII lookalikes separately.
72	func isASCIIFoldOf(key, canonical string) bool {
73		if len(key) != len(canonical) {
74			return false
75		}
76		for i := 0; i < len(key); i++ {
77			c := key[i]
78			if c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' {
79				c += 'a' - 'A'
80			}
81			if c != canonical[i] {
82				return false
83			}
84		}
85		return true
86	}

88	// isJobVersionKey reports whether key names a job record's pinned circuit
89	// version field under any spelling the ordinary decode fills Version from:
90	// canonical "version", an ASCII letter-case variant such as "VERSION" or
91	// "VeRsIoN", or a JSON-escaped spelling that unescapes onto either. Because
92	// encoding/json's struct-tag matching folds with Unicode case rules
93	// (strings.EqualFold), the long-s "verſion" (U+017F, written directly or as
94	// the u017f escape) names the field too.
95	func isJobVersionKey(key string) bool {
96		return strings.EqualFold(key, jobVersionKey)
97	}

100	// field under any spelling the ordinary decode fills Circuit from: canonical
101	// "circuit" or an ASCII letter-case variant such as "CIRCUIT" or "CiRcUiT",
102	// including a JSON-escaped spelling that unescapes onto either (keys arrive
103	// here already unescaped). No non-ASCII rune case-folds onto any letter of
104	// "circuit", so the ASCII fold and encoding/json's Unicode-folded tag
105	// matching recognize exactly the same keys for this field.
106	func isJobCircuitKey(key string) bool {
107		return isASCIIFoldOf(key, jobCircuitKey)
108	}
109	
110	// isJobIDKey reports whether key names a job record's identity field under
111	// any spelling the ordinary decode fills ID from: canonical "id" and the
112	// ASCII letter-case variants "ID", "Id", "iD", including a JSON-escaped
113	// spelling that unescapes onto one of them (keys arrive here already

122	// compiled-artifact binding field: only "compiled_hash" itself and ASCII
123	// letter-case variants such as "COMPILED_HASH" or "CoMpIlEd_HaSh". Non-ASCII

129	// rejectAmbiguousJobID enforces the identity uniqueness rule shared by the
130	// directory scan and the single-record decode (both drive readJobRecord):
131	// the id is a job's sole, deterministic identity — the key a query uses to
132	// find the record — so one record may carry the field under at most one
133	// recognized spelling (isJobIDKey): canonical "id", the ASCII letter-case
134	// variants "ID", "Id", "iD", or a JSON-escaped spelling that unescapes onto
135	// one of them. Two spellings on one record make the job's identity depend on
136	// key order, since encoding/json keeps the last value, and corrupt the read:
137	// the whole record is refused whether the values agree or differ, whether
138	// both are present, non-empty and legal ids, and whether unrelated members
139	// (the circuit name, the pinned version, the attempt count, …) sit between
140	// them — neither value is ever picked to carry on, and swapping the two keys
141	// never changes the refusal or moves the query id. A record carrying only
142	// case variants with no lowercase "id" ("ID" beside "Id", …) is refused on
143	// the same terms: the pair still names one field twice. Two byte-identical
144	// spellings are covered too. A single spelling of any recognized kind is the
145	// one id field and keeps its current reading: the value is matched exactly
146	// as written, with no case folding, space trimming or U+FFFD repair.

213	// most one recognized spelling (isJobCircuitKey). Two spellings on one record

215	// last value, and corrupt the read: the whole record is refused whether the
216	// values agree or differ, whether both name legal circuits, and whether
217	// unrelated members (the version, the attempt count, …) sit between them —
218	// neither value is ever picked to carry on, and swapping the two keys never
219	// changes the refusal. A single spelling of any recognized kind is the one
220	// circuit field and keeps its current reading: the value is matched against
221	// circuit names exactly as written, with no case folding or space trimming.
222	//
223	// keys are the record's member keys in any order; the recognized spellings are
224	// filtered and sorted here so the message is deterministic. where names the
225	// record exactly as the calling read path already located it (by id when the
226	// scan read one, else by position), so both paths name the problem the same
227	// way.
228	func rejectAmbiguousJobCircuit(where string, keys []string) error {
229		var circuitKeys []string
230		for _, key := range keys {
231			if isJobCircuitKey(key) {
232				circuitKeys = append(circuitKeys, key)
233			}
234		}
235		if len(circuitKeys) <= 1 {
236			return nil
237		}
238		sort.Strings(circuitKeys)
239		quoted := make([]string, len(circuitKeys))
240		for i, k := range circuitKeys {
241			quoted[i] = strconv.Quote(k)
242		}
243		return corruptf("%s carries the circuit field %q more than once (as %s)",
244			where, jobCircuitKey, strings.Join(quoted, ", "))
245	}
246	
247	// compiledHashLookalike reports a member key encoding/json would match onto
248	// the binding field's struct tag yet which is not an accepted ASCII spelling
249	// (isCompiledHashKey). Struct-tag matching in encoding/json folds with the
250	// Unicode simple case-folding rules, so a non-ASCII lookalike —
251	// "compiled_haſh" with U+017F long s, whether written directly or as the
252	// JSON escape u017f — silently fills CompiledHash and would let a damaged
253	// binding (null above all) read as unbound, then vanish on the next commit.
254	// Such a key is damage, regardless of its value or of a correctly spelled
255	// sibling key being present. Several aliases are reported in lexicographic
256	// order so the message is stable.
257	func compiledHashLookalike(keys []string) string {
258		var aliases []string
259		for _, key := range keys {
260			if isCompiledHashKey(key) {
261				continue
262			}
263			if strings.EqualFold(key, compiledHashKey) {
264				aliases = append(aliases, key)
265			}
266		}
267		if len(aliases) == 0 {
268			return ""
269		}
270		sort.Strings(aliases)
271		return aliases[0]
272	}
273	
274	// jobMember is one member of a saved job record as seen during the single
275	// per-record pass: its already-unescaped key and its raw value.
276	type jobMember struct {
277		key   string
278		value json.RawMessage
279	}
280	
281	// jobRecordScan is the one read of one saved job record. Both read passes —
282	// the envelope-wide duplicate-key scan (scanJobArray) and the typed decode
283	// (decodeJob) — build one through readJobRecord. It records only what the
284	// shared rules need: the members in document order (exact spelling), the
285	// first member key repeated under that same exact spelling, the best-effort
286	// id used to name the record, any duplicate key nested inside a member's
287	// own object/array value, exact-readback damage to the id token, and the raw
288	// circuit token whose exact-readback check judge runs (invalid UTF-8 bytes
289	// or an unpaired \uXXXX surrogate). Turning the members into a typed
290	// persistJob is left to the ordinary struct decode, which runs once
291	// afterwards.
292	type jobRecordScan struct {
293		positional     string
294		members        []jobMember
295		dupKey         string
296		id             string
297		nestedErr      error
298		idEncodingErr  error
299		circuitTok     json.RawMessage
300		circuitTokSeen bool
301	}
302	
303	// scanName locates the record for a directory-scan finding: by its id when an
304	// exact "id" spelling held a legible, reliably readable string, else by its
305	// 1-based position. The id probe is deliberately exact — an "ID" case
306	// variant is not the id for scan attribution — and is best-effort: a missing,
307	// non-string or undecodable id, or one whose bytes encoding/json would repair
308	// on decode (invalid UTF-8, an unpaired surrogate), leaves the positional
309	// name, since such an id cannot be recovered to quote faithfully.
310	func (r *jobRecordScan) scanName() string {
311		if r.id != "" && r.idEncodingErr == nil {
312			return fmt.Sprintf("stored job record %q", r.id)
313		}
314		return r.positional
315	}
316	
317	func (r *jobRecordScan) memberKeys() []string {
318		keys := make([]string, 0, len(r.members))
319		for _, m := range r.members {
320			keys = append(keys, m.key)
321		}
322		return keys
323	}
324	
325	func (r *jobRecordScan) valueOf(key string) json.RawMessage {
326		for _, m := range r.members {
327			if m.key == key {
328				return m.value
329			}
330		}
331		return nil
332	}
333	
334	// bindingKeys lists the record's accepted compiled_hash spellings (canonical
335	// and ASCII case variants), in document order.
336	func (r *jobRecordScan) bindingKeys() []string {
337		var keys []string
338		for _, m := range r.members {
339			if isCompiledHashKey(m.key) {
340				keys = append(keys, m.key)
341			}
342		}
343		return keys
344	}
345	
346	// readJobRecord consumes exactly one job record value the decoder is
347	// positioned at — including its opening token — and returns the single scan.
348	// Every token is consumed whether or not the record is damaged. A null
349	// element or a non-object element is structural damage named by positional.
350	// positional is the name used when no legible id is read: the directory scan
351	// passes "job record #<1-based index>", the typed decode passes
352	// "stored job record".
353	func readJobRecord(dec *json.Decoder, positional string) (*jobRecordScan, error) {
354		open, err := dec.Token()
355		if err != nil {
356			return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: %v", positional, err)
357		}
358		if open == nil {
359			return nil, corruptf("%s must be a JSON object, not null", positional)
360		}
361		if open != json.Delim('{') {
362			return nil, corruptf("%s must be a JSON object", positional)
363		}
364	
365		r := &jobRecordScan{positional: positional}
366		seenExact := make(map[string]bool)
367		for dec.More() {
368			keyTok, err := dec.Token()
369			if err != nil {
370				return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: %v", positional, err)
371			}
372			key, ok := keyTok.(string)
373			if !ok {
374				return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON", positional)
375			}
376			// Consume the whole value first; the judgments below use only the key
377			// (and, for the id probe, the already-captured bytes). Job members are
378			// scalars, but an unknown member may carry an object/array whose own
379			// duplicate keys must still fail the read.
380			var value json.RawMessage
381			if err := dec.Decode(&value); err != nil {
382				return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: %v", positional, err)
383			}
384			// The id is the job's identity and must read back exactly as the
385			// bytes on disk carry it. encoding/json silently rewrites invalid
386			// UTF-8 bytes and unpaired \uXXXX surrogate escapes to U+FFFD, so the
387			// raw token of every spelling the ordinary decode fills ID from
388			// (isJobIDKey: canonical "id" and the ASCII case variants "ID",
389			// "Id", "iD") is judged after the read. The exact "id" token also
390			// supplies the best-effort name used to locate the record. A
391			// non-string value (null, a number …) is left to the ordinary
392			// decode's own failure: the encoding walk below is defined only over
393			// one complete JSON string token.
394			isIDSpelling := isJobIDKey(key)
395			if isIDSpelling && bytes.HasPrefix(bytes.TrimSpace(value), []byte{'"'}) {
396				if key == jobIDKey {
397					if idVal, ierr := storedRecordShape.string(value, positional+` field "id"`); ierr == nil {
398						r.id = idVal
399					}
400				}
401				// The field is always quoted by its canonical name "id" in the
402				// diagnostic, whatever accepted spelling the damaged token was
403				// written under (an "ID" variant, a \uXXXX-escaped key).
404				if r.idEncodingErr == nil {
405					r.idEncodingErr = checkStoredStringEncoding(value,
406						positional+` field "id"`, "committed job id")
407				}
408			}
409			// The circuit a job belongs to is the sole authority for which frozen
410			// version, trusted setup and compiled artifact the job is read
411			// against, so its saved token must read back exactly too. The token
412			// of every spelling the ordinary decode fills Circuit from
413			// (isJobCircuitKey: canonical "circuit", the ASCII case variants
414			// "CIRCUIT", "CiRcUiT", …, and any JSON-escaped spelling of them) is
415			// captured and judged in judge, where an intact id still names the
416			// record — unlike a damaged id, a damaged circuit value does not make
417			// the job unnameable. Invalid UTF-8 bytes or an unpaired \uXXXX
418			// surrogate would otherwise be silently rewritten to U+FFFD, so a
419			// damaged value could collide with a circuit that genuinely contains
420			// "�" and borrow that circuit's frozen version, setup and compiled
421			// artifact. Two recognized spellings are already refused above by
422			// rejectAmbiguousJobCircuit, which outranks this check; the first
423			// recognized token therefore is the one circuit field. A non-string
424			// value (null, a number …) is left to the ordinary decode's own
425			// failure: the encoding walk is defined only over one complete JSON
426			// string token.
427			if isJobCircuitKey(key) && !r.circuitTokSeen &&
428				bytes.HasPrefix(bytes.TrimSpace(value), []byte{'"'}) {
429				r.circuitTok = value
430				r.circuitTokSeen = true
431			}
432			if seenExact[key] && r.dupKey == "" {
433				r.dupKey = key
434			}
435			seenExact[key] = true
436			r.members = append(r.members, jobMember{key: key, value: value})
437			trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(value)
438			if r.nestedErr == nil && len(trimmed) > 0 && (trimmed[0] == '{' || trimmed[0] == '[') {
439				nd := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(trimmed))
440				r.nestedErr = skipValueWithDupKeys(nd, positional+" field "+strconv.Quote(key))
441			}
442		}
443		if closeTok, err := dec.Token(); err != nil || closeTok != json.Delim('}') {
444			return nil, corruptf("%s is not valid JSON", positional)
445		}
446		return r, nil
447	}
448	
449	// judge applies the findings the directory scan owns, in the order they
450	// surface:
451	//
452	//  1. two recognized spellings of the job id field — equal or differing
453	//     values, both present and legal, even with unrelated members interleaved
454	//     and even with no lowercase "id" among them — so the job's identity is
455	//     never chosen by key order; this finding names the record positionally
456	//     (r.positional), never by a candidate id, because the record itself
457	//     refuses to settle which value that is;
458	//  2. two recognized spellings of the pinned version field — equal or
459	//     differing values, both legal, even with unrelated members interleaved —
460	//     so the bound version is never chosen by key order;
461	//  3. two recognized spellings of the owning circuit field, under the same
462	//     rule — the circuit a job belongs to is never chosen by key order;
463	//  4. an exact repeated member key (the first such key in document order,
464	//     including two byte-identical keys a member map could not retain);
465	//  5. a duplicate key nested inside a member's own object/array value;
466	//  6. an id token that would not read back unchanged — invalid UTF-8 bytes
467	//     or an unpaired surrogate escape under the canonical "id" or any ASCII
468	//     case spelling of it — so a saved job can never be re-read under a
469	//     U+FFFD-repaired identity; the record is located positionally when the
470	//     id itself cannot be recovered faithfully;
471	//  7. a circuit token that would likewise not read back unchanged — invalid
472	//     UTF-8 bytes or an unpaired surrogate escape under the canonical
473	//     "circuit" or any ASCII case/JSON-escaped spelling of it — so a saved
474	//     job's owning circuit is never repaired into another circuit's name and
475	//     never borrows that circuit's frozen version, trusted setup or compiled
476	//     artifact.
477	//
478	// The binding-field lookalike, duplicate-binding and binding-value-type rules
479	// are deliberately not here: the typed decode (which runs after the scan) owns
480	// those, so the historical precedence — every scan finding outranking every
481	// binding finding — is preserved when several problems coexist.
482	func (r *jobRecordScan) judge(where string) error {
483		if err := rejectAmbiguousJobID(r.positional, r.memberKeys()); err != nil {
484			return err
485		}
486		if err := rejectAmbiguousJobVersion(where, r.memberKeys()); err != nil {
487			return err
488		}
489		if err := rejectAmbiguousJobCircuit(where, r.memberKeys()); err != nil {
490			return err
491		}
492		if r.dupKey != "" {
493			return corruptf("%s contains duplicate field %q", where, r.dupKey)
494		}
495		if r.nestedErr != nil {
496			return r.nestedErr
497		}
498		if r.idEncodingErr != nil {
499			return r.idEncodingErr
500		}
501		if r.circuitTokSeen {
502			// Run the walk at judgment time so the diagnostic names the record
503			// through where — by its id when the id read back intact, else by
504			// record position — and always quotes the field by its canonical
505			// name "circuit", whatever accepted spelling carried the token.
506			if err := checkStoredStringEncoding(r.circuitTok,
507				where+` field "circuit"`, "committed owning circuit name"); err != nil {
508				return err
509			}
510		}
511		return nil
512	}
513	
514	// scanJobArray consumes one "jobs" value positioned at its opening bracket and
515	// reads every record through the shared per-record engine, judging each before
516	// moving on. It is the directory-read counterpart of decodeJob and exists so a
517	// structural problem inside one job is attributed to that job — by its id when
518	// the id is a legible string that reads back unchanged, else by its 1-based
519	// position — rather than to an opaque "jobs" element index. A null array
520	// stays the pre-existing "no jobs" reading.
521	func scanJobArray(dec *json.Decoder) error {
522		tok, err := dec.Token()
523		if err != nil {
524			return corruptf("data file envelope field \"jobs\" is not valid JSON: %v", err)
525		}
526		if tok == nil { // null: json.Unmarshal would produce no jobs
527			return nil
528		}
529		if tok != json.Delim('[') {
530			return corruptf("data file envelope field \"jobs\" must be an array")
531		}
532		index := 0
533		for dec.More() {
534			index++
535			r, err := readJobRecord(dec, fmt.Sprintf("job record #%d", index))
536			if err != nil {
537				return err
538			}
539			if err := r.judge(r.scanName()); err != nil {
540				return err
541			}
542		}
543		if closeTok, err := dec.Token(); err != nil || closeTok != json.Delim(']') {
544			return corruptf("data file envelope field \"jobs\" is not valid JSON")
545		}
546		return nil
547	}
548	
549	// Strict decoding of a committed job record, including its identity id and its
550	// compiled-artifact binding.
551	//
552	// The id is the job's identity and is held to the same exact-readback rule as
553	// a circuit's name: its raw JSON string token must denote its value exactly —
554	// valid UTF-8 in its literal portions and no unpaired \uXXXX surrogate
555	// escapes under any spelling the ordinary decode fills ID from (canonical
556	// "id" and ASCII case variants such as "ID", a JSON-escaped spelling of
557	// either included). Both damage shapes decode to U+FFFD under encoding/json,
558	// so the job would read back under a repaired identity — a follow-up GetJob
559	// by the submitted id would miss it, and it could collide with an id that
560	// genuinely contains "�". Such a record is data corruption: the read is
561	// refused (named by record position when the id cannot be recovered
562	// faithfully), no partial results are returned and the file is never
563	// rewritten. A real "�", a correctly paired surrogate and the literal text
564	// \uD800 all stay ordinary ids. The shared readJobRecord engine judges this
565	// for both read passes.
566	//
567	// compiled_hash is a field whose presence is meaningful: records written
568	// before bindings existed simply omit it, and an explicit "" is the unbound
569	// state. But once the key appears its value must be a JSON string. A null is
570	// not "no binding" — it is damage to a binding the record claims to carry,
571	// and so is a number, boolean, array or object in its place. Reading either
572	// as the zero string would silently turn a bound job into an unbound one
573	// (and the next commit would drop the field entirely), so the read is
574	// refused as data corruption instead. A legal non-empty string keeps being
575	// matched against the pinned version's artifact by validateEnvelope, exactly
576	// as written.
577	//
578	// The field is recognized under any ASCII letter-case spelling, so a record
579	// carrying "COMPILED_HASH" (or any mixed-case form, escaped or not) is the
580	// same binding and follows the same rules: a single such key is read with
581	// the full string validation, and two spellings of the field on one record —
582	// even with byte-identical values — are a duplicate binding and corrupt the
583	// read rather than being resolved by key order.
584	//
585	// Non-ASCII spellings are not accepted even though encoding/json itself
586	// would fold them onto the field: its struct-tag matching uses Unicode case
587	// folding, under which "compiled_haſh" (U+017F long s, written directly or
588	// as the JSON escape u017f) names CompiledHash just like "compiled_hash".
589	// Such a lookalike is damage to the binding the record claims to carry and
590	// is refused whatever its value — null, a legal hash or an explicit "" —
591	// and even when a correctly spelled "compiled_hash" sits beside it, in
592	// either key order and whether the two values agree. The damaged binding
593	// must never read as an unbound job and disappear on the next commit.
594	//
595	// The pinned version field is held to its own uniqueness rule
596	// (rejectAmbiguousJobVersion): every spelling the ordinary decode fills
597	// Version from counts as that one field (isJobVersionKey): canonical
598	// "version", an ASCII letter-case variant such as "VERSION", and, since
599	// struct-tag matching folds with Unicode case rules, the long-s "verſion"
600	// (U+017F, direct or u017f-escaped). Two such spellings on one record are
601	// refused as data corruption whether the values agree or differ, whether
602	// both values are legal versions, and even when unrelated fields are
603	// interleaved between them. A non-ASCII "verſion" is refused only when
604	// another recognized spelling sits beside it; appearing by itself it is the
605	// single version field and keeps the current reading (the ordinary decode
606	// folds it onto Version). An illegal single value — a string, a float,
607	// null, or a non-positive version — is rejected exactly as before, by the
608	// ordinary decode or validateEnvelope.
609	//
610	// The owning circuit field is held to its own uniqueness rule
611	// (rejectAmbiguousJobCircuit): every spelling the ordinary decode fills
612	// Circuit from counts as that one field (isJobCircuitKey): canonical
613	// "circuit" and ASCII letter-case variants such as "CIRCUIT" or "CiRcUiT",
614	// JSON-escaped spellings included. Two such spellings on one record are
615	// refused as data corruption whether the values agree or differ, whether
616	// both name legal frozen circuits with trusted setups, and even when
617	// unrelated fields are interleaved between them — the job's owning circuit
618	// is never resolved by key order. A single recognized spelling keeps the
619	// current reading, and the value keeps being matched against circuit names
620	// exactly as written: "alpha" and "ALPHA" stay distinct circuits and no
621	// whitespace is trimmed.
622	//
623	// Beyond uniqueness, that one circuit value carries the same exact-readback
624	// rule the id does: its raw JSON string token must denote the owning circuit
625	// exactly — valid UTF-8 in its literal portions and no unpaired \uXXXX
626	// surrogate escapes under every spelling isJobCircuitKey recognizes. Both
627	// damage shapes decode to U+FFFD under encoding/json, so without the check a
628	// job saved with a truncated multi-byte sequence or a lone \uD800 escape
629	// could read back as if it named a different circuit that genuinely contains
630	// "�" — and, when that other version is frozen with a trusted setup and a
631	// compiled artifact, the job would then successfully borrow its version,
632	// setup and artifact. The owning circuit must be determined by the saved
633	// bytes alone, so such a record is data corruption: the read is refused,
634	// named by the job (by its id when legible, else by record position) and the
635	// circuit field, even when the repaired name exists and everything it would
636	// resolve to is in place. A legal Chinese or emoji value, an actually
637	// committed "�", a correctly paired surrogate and the literal six-character
638	// text \uD800 are all ordinary circuit values that keep their exact spelling.
639	//
640	// The identity field is held to the same uniqueness rule, and with the
641	// strictest attribution (rejectAmbiguousJobID): every spelling the ordinary
642	// decode fills ID from counts as that one field (isJobIDKey) — canonical
643	// "id", the three ASCII letter-case variants "ID", "Id" and "iD", and a
644	// JSON-escaped spelling that unescapes onto any of them; "id" has no
645	// non-ASCII case fold, so those four are exactly the recognized spellings.
646	// Two such spellings on one record make the job's query id a function of
647	// key order (encoding/json keeps the last value) and are refused as data
648	// corruption whether the two values agree or differ, whether both are
649	// present, non-empty and legal ids (legal Chinese, emoji and "�" included),
650	// even when unrelated fields (circuit, version, attempt, …) are interleaved
651	// between them, and even when neither spelling is the lowercase "id"
652	// ("ID" beside "Id", …) — no combination of variants bypasses the rule and
653	// two byte-identical spellings stay refused as well. Because the record
654	// then has no settled identity, the error locates it by its 1-based position
655	// in the jobs array ("job record #n") rather than quoting either candidate
656	// value, and names the field by its canonical name "id". A single
657	// recognized spelling keeps the current reading, and its value continues to
658	// match exactly as written: no case folding, trimming or U+FFFD repair.
659	//
660	// The shared readJobRecord scan enforces every key and structural rule once
661	// for both read passes; after it clears, this decode applies the rules the
662	// scan cannot — the binding-field lookalike, at-most-one binding and its
663	// string type — and then runs the ordinary struct decode for every other
664	// job field.
665	func (j *persistJob) UnmarshalJSON(raw []byte) error {
666		const what = "stored job record"
667		return decodeJob(raw, what, j)
668	}
669	
670	// decodeJob reads one saved job record from raw through the shared engine and
671	// fills out. what is the generic name for a record with no legible id.
672	func decodeJob(raw []byte, what string, out *persistJob) error {
673		trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(raw)
674		if len(trimmed) == 0 {
675			return corruptf("%s must be a JSON object", what)
676		}
677		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(trimmed))
678		r, err := readJobRecord(dec, what)
679		if err != nil {
680			return err
681		}
682		// A single complete object is the whole record, checked before any field
683		// is judged (the old strict member walk led with shape and trailing-data
684		// checks). At open this is already guaranteed by the directory scan; the
685		// check keeps the single-record decode self-contained.
686		if _, err := dec.Token(); err != io.EOF {
687			return corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: trailing data after the object", what)
688		}
689	
690		// Name the record the way this pass always has: an ordinary struct probe
691		// folds id spellings the same way the final decode does (so an "ID"
692		// variant still names the record), and a missing or non-string id leaves
693		// the generic name. The probe only labels errors; the id is decoded for
694		// real by the ordinary pass below. An id whose bytes encoding/json would
695		// repair (invalid UTF-8, an unpaired surrogate) is never quoted: it cannot
696		// be recovered faithfully, so the generic positional name stands and the
697		// idEncodingErr message below locates the record and field by position.
698		where := what
699		var idProbe struct {
700			ID string `json:"id"`
701		}
702		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &idProbe); err == nil && idProbe.ID != "" && r.idEncodingErr == nil {
703			where = fmt.Sprintf("stored job record %q", idProbe.ID)
704		}
705	
706		// The scan-owned findings (id, version and circuit ambiguity, exact and
707		// nested duplicate keys) outrank every binding finding, exactly as when
708		// the directory scan ran ahead of this decode. (During an open the scan
709		// has already enforced them, so this is a no-op there; it keeps the
710		// single-record decoder self-contained.) The id-ambiguity finding is
711		// always attributed positionally inside judge, so the probe-derived
712		// "where" (which may fold an "ID" variant) never labels a record that
713		// carries two ids with one of them.
714		if err := r.judge(where); err != nil {
715			return err
716		}
717	
718		// Reject a non-ASCII spelling that encoding/json's Unicode-folded tag
719		// matching would silently read as this field ("compiled_haſh" with long
720		// s, directly written or ſ-escaped), whatever its value and whether or
721		// not a correctly spelled key accompanies it. It must never be ignored as
722		// an unknown member, which would let a damaged binding read unbound.
723		if alias := compiledHashLookalike(r.memberKeys()); alias != "" {
724			return corruptf("%s carries the binding field %q under non-ASCII spelling %q; such a lookalike spelling is data corruption",
725				where, compiledHashKey, alias)
726		}
727		// Every accepted spelling of the binding field counts as the same one
728		// field; the record may carry it at most once, however it is capitalized.
729		bindingKeys := r.bindingKeys()
730		if len(bindingKeys) > 1 {
731			sort.Strings(bindingKeys)
732			quoted := make([]string, len(bindingKeys))
733			for i, k := range bindingKeys {
734				quoted[i] = strconv.Quote(k)
735			}
736			return corruptf("%s carries the binding field %q more than once (as %s)",
737				where, compiledHashKey, strings.Join(quoted, ", "))
738		}
739		compiledHash := ""
740		hasBinding := false
741		if len(bindingKeys) == 1 {
742			// The field is always quoted by its canonical name in the diagnostic,
743			// regardless of the accepted spelling it was written under.
744			hash, err := storedRecordShape.string(r.valueOf(bindingKeys[0]), where+` field "compiled_hash"`)
745			if err != nil {
746				return err
747			}
748			compiledHash, hasBinding = hash, true
749		}
750		// With zero or one recognized version spelling, the ordinary decode below
751		// already yields the current value: a single canonical/ASCII/long-s
752		// spelling folds onto Version, and a missing version reads as 0 and is
753		// rejected by validateEnvelope as a job bound to an unknown circuit. Illegal
754		// single values (a string, a float, null, zero or negative) keep being
755		// rejected by that same decode or the envelope validation, so nothing is
756		// picked here.
757		type plainJob persistJob
758		var decoded plainJob
759		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &decoded); err != nil {
760			return corruptf("%s is not valid JSON: %v", what, err)
761		}
762		if hasBinding {
763			decoded.CompiledHash = compiledHash
764		}
765		*out = persistJob(decoded)
766		return nil
767	}

19	// negative. The name must additionally be complete, valid UTF-8: it is the
20	// version's identity and is looked up by exact value, and encoding/json
21	// silently rewrites invalid byte sequences (a lone continuation byte, a
22	// truncated multi-byte character, …) to U+FFFD when the record is marshaled,
23	// so accepting them would save the circuit under a different name than the
24	// caller submitted. Such a request is refused as ErrInvalidArgument before
25	// anything is committed. Creating an already-existing version is idempotent
26	// when the description is identical (the stored record is returned
27	// unchanged); a differing description is reported as ErrConflict. Nothing
28	// about an existing version — frozen or not — is ever replaced by Create.
29	func (s *Store) CreateCircuit(c Circuit) (Circuit, error) {
30		if err := validateCircuitKey(c.Name, c.Version); err != nil {

35		}

37			return Circuit{}, err
38		}

41		err := s.withLock(func() (bool, error) {
42			if existing := findCircuit(s.data.Circuits, c.Name, c.Version); existing != nil {
43				if existing.Description != c.Description {
44					return false, conflictf("circuit %q version %d already exists with a different description", c.Name, c.Version)
45				}

47				return false, nil
48			}

51				Constraints: c.Constraints, PublicInputs: c.PublicInputs, PrivateInputs: c.PrivateInputs,
52				Frozen: false, Description: c.Description,
53			}
54			s.data.Circuits = append(s.data.Circuits, record)

Done. The vulnerability is fixed — a saved setup record whose `name` carries damaged encoding can no longer be repaired onto a different circuit's name.

## Changes

**Read path — `zkcircuit/setup_record.go`** (`judgeSetupRecord`, run by `scanSetupArray` on every load via `Open`/`withLock`/`withLockRead`):
- While tokenizing each setup record, the raw JSON value of every recognized name-key spelling is captured (`isSetupNameKey` already covers canonical `"name"`, ASCII case variants like `"NAME"`/`"NaMe"`, and `\uXXXX`-escaped spellings — so no variant bypasses the check).
- After the existing name/version ambiguity, duplicate-key and nested-duplicate checks, the captured token goes through the existing `checkStoredStringEncoding` (the same exact-readback walk circuit names and job circuit/id fields already use). It rejects:
  - invalid literal UTF-8 (lone continuation bytes, truncated multi-byte, overlong/0xFF/encoded-surrogate-half bytes), and
  - unpaired `\uXXXX` high/low surrogate escapes (including reversed and post-pair ones).
- The error is `ErrDataCorrupt`, located as `setup record #N field "name"` (1-based position), so it is never misreported as "unknown circuit" or "missing trusted setup". Duplicate-name-key rejection outranks the new check, matching job-record precedence.

**Write path — `zkcircuit/operations.go`** (`RecordSetup`): rejects a non-valid-UTF-8 name with `ErrInvalidArgument` (exit 1 on the CLI) before taking the lock or committing, mirroring `CreateCircuit`/`SubmitJob`.

Because every operation re-reads and fully validates `data.json` under the lock, the rule covers queries (no partial results from other records), setup registration and job submission (no success, file kept byte-for-byte), and handles already-open stores on their next operation. The CLI already maps `ErrDataCorrupt` to exit code 3 with "read failed".

**Untouched behavior:** legal Chinese/emoji/genuine `�`/paired surrogates/literal `\uD800` text read back by exact value; exact matching (no trimming/case-folding), the existing name-field duplicate rule, duplicate registration and proof-job setup gating all keep their prior behavior.

**Tests added:** `zkcircuit/setup_name_encoding_test.go` (motivating collision against a frozen `电路�` circuit with a proof job, all invalid-UTF-8/surrogate shapes, key-spelling variants, second-record position, open-handle refusal with byte preservation, write-path rejection, legal round-trips, exact matching) and `cmd/zkcircuit/corrupt_setup_name_encoding_cli_test.go` (exit 3/no output/byte-preservation across all data commands, key spellings, position #2, exit 1 for invalid `setup-record`, Unicode round-trip). Full suite and `go vet` pass.
